cards.explanation: The answer is hands, friends. The Pharisees and scribes, religious leaders who came from Jerusalem, say, “They do not wash their hands before they eat.” That's the whole charge. They call it breaking the tradition of the elders, which is a big name for a very small sink moment.

The answer is that Jesus asks why they break the command of God for their tradition. He replies, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?” They asked about the elders' tradition, and He asks about God's command. Same question shape, but now it's pointed the other way, and I think that landed in the room like a dropped tray.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’…” That's the first command He points to. Then He adds a second one right behind it, about anyone who curses his father or mother. He's reaching for God's words, not the elders' words.

The answer is False. Their teaching says that once he says it's a gift devoted to God, “…he need not honor his father or mother with it.” So he doesn't have to honor them with it. Jesus says this is how they nullify the word of God for the sake of their tradition, because God's command said to honor your father and mother.

The answer is far from Him, friends. The words say, “These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.” The lips are in the room and the heart is out the door. Jesus says Isaiah, Israel's prophet, prophesied correctly about them.

The answer is men. The words say, “They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.” So the rules they're teaching come from people. That's the thread running through this whole conversation.

The answer is what comes out of his mouth. Jesus tells the crowd, “A man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it.” I sample every batch I bake, so this was a relief to hear. The focus moves from the plate to what comes out.

The answer is that they were offended. The disciples tell Jesus, “Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?” I think the disciples were a little nervous bringing it up. That's the kind of news you deliver quietly.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.” Notice it's both of them, not just the follower. He says this right after calling the Pharisees blind guides.

The answer is that Jesus asks if they still don't understand. Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, asks Him to explain the parable. Jesus asks first, “Do you still not understand?” Peter asked for help and got a question before the answer. I know that feeling too.

The answer is into the stomach and then out, friends. Jesus says, “…whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated?” So food takes a trip through and out. Then He says the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart (Matthew 15:18).

The answer is heart. Jesus says, “But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man.” The mouth is just the doorway, and the heart is where it starts. That connects right back to the Isaiah words about hearts far from God.

The answer is evil thoughts and theft, and both are on His list. Jesus says, “…evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.” This is a heavy list, friends. Jesus says these come out of the heart.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “These are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him.” So unwashed hands do not defile a man. It's the same hands the Pharisees and scribes started with, and He's come all the way back to the first question and answered it.
